# Security review: PR #253, final round

Head: d992f6747b492e6dd80237d38ecc236d4cdca981
Reviewed delta: ac8a00daf5c0ca017d4fc858e4a0eee5ae72e913..d992f6747b492e6dd80237d38ecc236d4cdca981
Result: pass

No new security vulnerabilities found in the reviewed delta under C33. Both round-1 security findings are closed. This is the final round under C34; there are no outstanding security findings or security note-owed items.

## Round-1 findings closed

1. Close-command quoting: CLOSED. The shared constructor applies shell_word separately to the complete seat and pane arguments (crates/daemon/src/spawn_waits.rs:85-90); HTTP delegates to it (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1933-1936). The regression uses spaces and shell metacharacters (spawn_waits.rs:540-550).

2. Spawn-id-only notification consumption: CLOSED. The original launch seat and pane must match before an entry is marked bound or removed (spawn_waits.rs:163-179). The wrong-seat/pane regression verifies that mismatches leave the legitimate handoff available (spawn_waits.rs:513-522).

## Attribution and data handling

- Active launches snapshot request.parent and persist that parent in the seat descriptor (http/mod.rs:1638-1662). Notices use stored Launch.parent, not the registering descriptor's parent (spawn_waits.rs:312-340). At boot the snapshot is reconstructed from persisted row metadata (spawn_waits.rs:67-73), not immutable launch-event metadata; no stronger provenance claim is made.
- The new launch, answer and report payloads carry launch identifiers, attribution, outcome/reason, quoted close command and receipt/withheld metadata, not new environment, argv, token or captured-output fields (http/mod.rs:1953-1958; spawn_waits.rs:307-356).
- The round-1 raw-startup-output alert remains withdrawn as retained baseline behavior. This verdict does not claim that arbitrary existing startup diagnostics are comprehensively redacted.
- R253-001/002 correctness closure and live resource-cost approval belong to their respective reviewers. This security verdict closes the quoting and launch-correlation findings only.

## Verification

- just pr-freeze 253: PASS immediately before publication preparation; remote and GitHub agree on the full head above, main base, CLEAN, ready, all five latest checks pass.
- GitHub Actions run 44457191062, attempt 2: SUCCESS at this exact head. Rust test job 135336560805 reports 2540 passed and 6 skipped. Rust lint and both Node check jobs also pass.
- Successful job 135336560805's upload log pins JUnit artifact 14498074181. The run has multiple artifacts named junit-linux; the successful job's ID was used, not name-only or newest-artifact selection.
- Downloaded artifact 14498074181 and parsed JUnit XML: all eight packet-named regressions are present and passed:
  - bind_then_drop_reports_once
  - bind_before_a_timeout_settles_reports_once
  - a_failure_then_a_late_bind_reports_once
  - an_answered_launch_is_never_reported
  - another_seat_or_pane_sharing_the_spawn_id_does_not_bind_it
  - a_recovered_launch_reports_when_bound
  - the_close_command_quotes_each_word
  - a_seat_bound_before_a_restart_cut_its_answer_is_reported_at_boot
- Attempt 1's only failure was the real-tmux control-mode test a_lost_control_client_falls_back_then_reconnects, reporting no server at crates/tmux/tests/control_mode.rs:381. Attempt 2 passed the full suite at the same head.
- No local build, test, mutation run, harness boot or harness checks was executed. CI evidence is not represented as a local harness run. The packet's absent route-level interrupted-bound-failure test is not a security blocker; the named unit interleaving regressions passed in CI.

## Harness feedback

Observation MW-001 in the security-253-r2 bucket captures the repeated manual work of selecting the successful job's exact artifact and proving named regressions ran. Candidate encoding: a read-only exact-head CI evidence command that resolves successful-job artifacts and returns named JUnit outcomes without running local tests. No product files were changed for this review.
